Lua Studio

Write, lint, statically analyse and (dry-run) deploy FortiWeb Web Scripting and FortiADC Scripting scripts, with a draft → tested → deployed lifecycle.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.lua_studio protection.apply
📍 WhereFortiWeb or FortiADC ADOM → Plugins → Lua Studio; Global ADOM → Administrator → Studio → Lua Studio (URL /lua/)

What is it?#

Lua Studio is an editor for the scripts that run on the appliances: FortiWeb Web Scripting (Lua) and FortiADC Scripting (an event-block language). It checks the script without running it, explains what it touches, keeps a simple lifecycle, and builds the request a deployment would send. Deployment is a dry run unless you explicitly confirm a real push.

What does it do?#

  • Lint: FortiWeb scripts are parse-checked with luac -p (compiled, never executed) and errors come back with line numbers. FortiADC scripts get a structural check instead — balanced parentheses and braces and at least one when <EVENT> { block — because they are not standalone Lua.
  • Static analysis: What it does (functions from a curated FortiWeb or FortiADC API list, such as reads a request header or redirects the client), Warnings (unterminated blocks, = inside a condition, os.execute / io.popen), calls not in the target API, line count and a binding hint.
  • Lifecycle: Draft → Tested → Deployed.
  • Deploy (dry-run): shows the request that would be sent — target, logical endpoint, content field and body — without contacting anything.
  • Deploy for real: pushes the script to the selected device.
  • Browse examples: example scripts for the chosen target.

Requirements#

  • A luac binary on the SATOM node (luac5.4, luac5.3, luac5.1 or luac). Without it, lint fails with luac not available on server — for FortiADC scripts too, even though they get only the structural check.
  • For a real deploy: a device selected on the script, reachable by SATOM.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open Lua Studio, create, edit, save, lint, change status, dry-run, delete studio.lua_studio
Deploy for real studio.lua_studio plus configuration-write (for example protection.apply, protection.edit, appliances.apply or another key that grants it)
Apply a Scout (AI assistant) Lua proposal as a draft advisor.use plus studio.lua_studio

studio.lua_studio is admin-only. Users without it get 403.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: scripts open only within their own ADOM; the Device list, save and deploy use only the devices visible to you; a real deploy without a device is refused instead of marking the script deployed; and the menu entries follow studio.lua_studio.

The menu entry — Plugins → Lua Studio in the FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs, Administrator → Studio → Lua Studio in the Global ADOM — is shown exactly to the users the page admits: holders of studio.lua_studio. No other permission (such as users.manage) is needed to see it: without users.manage the Global ADOM shows a standalone Studio group instead. The other device ADOMs show the entry greyed out (this product has no scripting object to deploy to).

How to use#

Write and check a script#

  1. Open Lua Studio and click FortiWeb or FortiADC to create a script for that target (the target cannot be changed later).
  2. Optional: Browse examples and insert one.
  3. Fill in Name, choose a Device (or — none (author only) —) and the Scripting object name used on the device (for example rewrite-legacy).
  4. Write the code in Lua code.
  5. Click Lint & analyse and read the Lint & static analysis panel.
  6. Click Save.

Move it through the lifecycle#

  1. Click Mark tested (lint gate). The lint runs again; if it passes the status becomes tested (Lint passed — marked tested.), otherwise it stays draft.
  2. Back to Draft returns it to draft at any time.
  3. Deployed can only be reached by a confirmed real push.

Deploy#

  1. Click Deploy (dry-run) to see the plan. Nothing is contacted and the status does not change. The plan is marked as not verified: the scripting wire format has not been confirmed against a live appliance.
  2. To push, select a Device on the script and Save, then click Deploy for real and confirm Push this script to the live device now?. The lint runs first; a failing script is refused. A script with no device is refused too and keeps its status — nothing is sent.

⚠️Warning

Real deployment is experimental. Review the dry-run body first.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Script name in SATOM Yes Block empty User-Agent
Device Appliance of the script's target kind that is visible to you; none = author only No fweb-01
Scripting object Object name on the device; defaults to the script name in the deploy plan No rewrite-legacy
Lua code Script body Yes see example

Example#

🧪Example — Block requests without a User-Agent (FortiWeb)

local ua = get_request_header("User-Agent")
if ua == nil then
  block()
end

Lint & analyse reports Lint passed and What it does: reads a request header, blocks the request, with the hint that Web Scripting is bound to a server policy through its scripting list.

Result#

  • Audit log entries: lua.save, lua.status, lua.deploy (with dry_run and the appliance) and lua.delete. Mark tested itself is not audited. See Audit log.
  • A real deploy without errors sets the status to deployed and records the time.

Troubleshooting#

"Lint failed — fix the reported errors first." / "Lint failed — fix the reported errors before marking tested."#

Possible causes - luac reported a syntax error (FortiWeb), or the structural check failed (FortiADC: unbalanced brackets or no event block).

Solution 1. Click Lint & analyse, fix each listed line, save, and try again.

"luac not available on server"#

Possible causes - No luac binary is installed on the SATOM node.

Solution 1. Install the Lua compiler package on the node.

"Lint failed — refusing to deploy."#

Possible causes - A deploy (dry-run or real) was requested for a script that does not lint.

"A name is required."#

Possible causes - Name was empty on save.

A real deploy reports an error#

Possible causes - The device rejected the request or was unreachable; the error is shown in the deploy result.

Solution 1. Check the dry-run body against the device's scripting object format, and the device's reachability.

"No target appliance: pick one in the editor and save before a real deploy."#

Possible causes - Deploy for real was confirmed on a script saved without a Device (— none (author only) —). Nothing is sent and the status does not change. The editor shows a red Deploy result with an empty body for this refusal.

Solution 1. Choose a Device, click Save, and deploy again.

Advanced#

Advanced What a deploy sends

FortiWeb scripts go to the server-policy scripting endpoint with the code in a content field; FortiADC scripts go to the system script endpoint with the code in a script field. The object name is the Scripting object (or the script name). The device's answer is shown truncated to 400 characters.

Advanced Scope

Scripts are stamped with the ADOM they were created in. The list, and opening, editing, deploying or deleting a script, work only on scripts of the ADOM you are in. The Device list shows the appliances of the script's target kind that are visible to you, and save and deploy accept only those devices.
